decisions.summary: Two sides, each its own denominator: the landings' side is every batch-keyed cell plus every `carry into the clone` cell; the tasks' side everything else but the GM's wait; two tables each ending in its own 100% row; the landings' side shows its categories.

decisions.summary: Every other percentage follows its side: carry rows and the second tier's table of the landings' working time, the rest of the tasks'; the GM's rows and the all row stay of the whole; The biggest blocking and The whole window become the tasks' side's.
decisions.why: This is the request applied to every percentage. Keeping the GM's rows of the whole is amendment (i) of 2026-11-25 left as it was. The wording should agree with D1, so that a carry booked to a task's key does not stay in the tasks' whole (0.8 min on the real window).

decisions.why: This is an implementation choice that changes no outcome the GM asked about. Every carry still lands on the landings' side, and leaving the booking alone keeps T298's 'a task's own table ends at its carry'.

decisions.summary: One cross-blocking row on the tasks' side, inside its blocking total, counting a task's wait on a landing: idle pool trees while a landing ran, and handouts refused while a done commit was not carried. Each second is counted once.
decisions.why: This is the request's 'except to the degree that things in one category actually are blocking things in the other category', for the direction the GM's message is about ('the implementation of our tasks in the builders was not blocked on this to the degree indicated'). The reverse direction needs no row. D1 puts every batch-keyed cell on the landings' side, so a landing's own waits are already in its denominator. decisions.why: Each limit measures 'actually blocking': idle time with no later demand, or beyond the pool's cap, is not a task waiting. Overcounting where the queue state is unknown is stated on the line, not hidden.

decisions.summary: Whether the queue held a READY entry while a tree stood free is not in the records. A later handout is taken to mean that work waited, and the line says it is an upper bound.
decisions.why: This inference overcounts, which errs toward showing blocking rather than hiding it, and it is said on the report's line. That matches amendment (l): 'it doesn't have to be 100% exact'.

decisions.why: That time already sits in the tasks' denominator, which is what the GM's exception asks for. Counting it again in the cross row would double it. It is named on the report's line.

decisions.summary: A builder's resume held by a gate is not counted, because no record ties a message's delivery to a landing. The report's line says so.
decisions.why: This is the one real task-on-landing wait the row leaves out, an undercount of the GM's 'to the degree that things ... actually are blocking'. It is legitimate on the GM's own words in amendment (l) of 2026-11-25: 'it doesn't have to be 100% exact ... what we're looking for here is just a broad understanding of where our time goes'.
